rapport_notes: Exceptionally warm and patient on an emotionally sensitive call (mother-in-law moving into a home-care studio, family still deciding); handled many tangents (military discount, company footprint) graciously.

evidence_quotes.agenda: "do you have any specific concerns or any important things that you wanted to answer during this call before we start?" -- asked right after the quid pro quo. Customer asked a real logistics question (pack-the-day-before-vs-move-day) that got a single direct factual answer with no further follow-up.
evidence_quotes.two_layers_deep: Customer: "when you guys come, do you come and pack up the day before and then move on the seventeenth or how does that work?" -- answered in one line ("normally if we need to pack then we will [pack] the day before moving") with no further digging.
evidence_quotes.save_your_ass: "it does not necessarily mean that you need to pay for nine hours or you're locked in for nine hours or six hours" -- pay-less-if-faster covered clearly.

top_strength: Built exceptional rapport and trust on a difficult, emotional call, which likely helped the family feel comfortable getting a full $4,423 worst-case quote before deciding.
coaching_note: No explicit close ask was made before the call ended (customer said she'd call back that evening) -- a light explicit ask (e.g. "want me to go ahead and hold the 17th while you decide?") could reduce the risk of losing the lead to a competitor during the gap.
